plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration breach and align with conservative limits.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and leverage.
The focus is on maintaining a stable book with minimal drawdown.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a potential target of ~1.5% per month. Risk is significantly reduced by eliminating leveraged ETFs and trimming concentration. Expect lower volatility and smaller drawdowns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach and align with balanced limits.
Reduce exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to small positions.
This reduces overall leverage while maintaining some growth potential.
Buy ALB at 4% as a strong new scanner setup to diversify and add quality.
balanced.read: This balanced plan prioritizes risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5% per month. Leverage is reduced but not eliminated, offering a blend of stability and growth. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach, maintaining aggressive concentration.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to press working names.
This strategy leans into leverage and concentration for higher growth potential.
Buy ALB at 6% as a strong new scanner setup, aligning with aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4% per month by stretching into leverage and concentration. Be aware that this significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lead to substantial losses quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
Sell all high-beta and leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to near zero.
This rotation prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
The focus is on creating a cash-like income stream, not growth.
income.read: This income plan aims to park cash for yield, targeting ~1% per month. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth by rotating into income ETFs. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
